title: Wall Street Opens Lower as AI Stocks Slide and Oil Climbs
excerpt: Nasdaq leads declines as CoreWeave and Nebius fall, Brent crude nears a five-month high around $111, and investors brace for SpaceX, Netflix, Meta and Tesla earnings.
body:
• Wall Street opened lower on Tuesday: the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 6.8 points, or 0.01%, to 51,959.21, the S&P 500 fell 11.7 points, or 0.15%, to 7,679.01, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 98.0 points, or 0.37%, to 26,332.92, according to Reuters.
  • AI infrastructure names led the decline, with CoreWeave down 3.1% and Nebius Group off 2.9% in premarket trading amid renewed concern over the debt used to finance the AI buildout.
  • Brent crude rose 1.7% to around $111 a barrel, near a five-month high, as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping in the Gulf.
  • Earnings set the agenda for the rest of the week: SpaceX and Netflix report after Tuesday's close, with Meta Platforms and Tesla due on Wednesday.

Wall Street's main indexes opened lower on Tuesday, dragged down by renewed weakness in AI-linked stocks and a rebound in oil prices, as investors braced for a heavy slate of corporate earnings this week.

At the open, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 6.8 points, or 0.01%, to 51,959.21, the S&P 500 fell 11.7 points, or 0.15%, to 7,679.01, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 98.0 points, or 0.37%, to 26,332.92, Reuters reported. The tech-heavy Nasdaq bore the brunt of the selling, extending a pattern in which AI-exposed names have swung sharply on financing concerns.

AI stocks retreat again

The declines followed a brief reprieve on Monday, when the S&P 500 and Nasdaq advanced as investors bought back into technology stocks after last week's sharp selloff, driven in part by concerns over CoreWeave's debt load and the cost of financing the AI buildout.

In premarket trading, CoreWeave dropped 3.1% and Nebius Group lost 2.9%, while Apple fell 1% and Nvidia slipped marginally, according to Reuters. Sentiment toward the sector was further dented overseas, where South Korean AI infrastructure company Elice Group tumbled nearly 30% in its market debut in Seoul, slipping below its IPO price after raising 201.1 billion won ($151.12 million).

"I see this as a dip inside a selective market rather than a genuine AI buying opportunity or the start of a deeper repricing. Investors are pickier about AI stories than they were a year ago."

— Ion Jauregui, analyst at ActivTrades, via Reuters

Oil climbs toward five-month high

Energy prices added to the cautious tone. Brent crude was up 1.7% at around $111 a barrel, near a five-month high, as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. Higher oil prices complicate the inflation outlook at a moment when investors are already questioning how much of the AI spending boom will translate into durable earnings.

Earnings in focus

Investors will now watch this week's corporate earnings for clues on whether technology companies can maintain strong growth in the face of mounting macroeconomic risks. Quarterly results from SpaceX and Netflix are due after the market close on Tuesday, while heavyweights Meta Platforms and Tesla are scheduled to report on Wednesday.

Among early movers, 3M shares rose 3.9% after the industrial conglomerate said it was expanding its commercial relationship with Amazon and had issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary allowing it to buy 3M common stock worth over $521 million. Steel Dynamics fell 6.3% after the steelmaker missed third-quarter profit estimates. General Motors, Hasbro, Halliburton and 3M were among the companies due to report before markets opened on Tuesday.

With the AI trade under scrutiny and oil near multi-month highs, traders said the earnings prints over the next two sessions — particularly guidance on data-center spending from Meta and Tesla — will likely determine whether Monday's rebound resumes or the selloff deepens.
